Subject: Private deployment — data residency & audit scope questions

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're excited about Redwood's Dedicated offering. A couple of compliance items came up on our side that we need to resolve before procurement will sign: 

- Data residency: Finoworks requires all customer data for this engagement to be physically stored and processed in US-only regions (no cross-border replication).
- Audit rights: our security team expects the right to perform an onsite audit or receive a broad set of logs beyond SOC2; they'd prefer full audit access to systems used for our tenant.
- Remote management constraints: we need assurance that remote admin access from Redwood-managed consoles can be restricted or disabled once deployed.

I've attached our RFP requirements (short summary). Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to US-only residency, what our options are for audit access (onsite vs attestation), and whether you can disable remote admin access for our environment?

Also note procurement will be pushing for a 35% first-year discount given the multi-year commitment and the bespoke deployment.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Grant
Director of Security & Compliance
Finoworks

Team — forwarding Finoworks' asks (see attached RFP). Quick summary of the non-standard items:

1) US-only residency (customer wants contractual pledge)
2) Onsite/full audit rights (they're asking for more than SOC2 scope)
3) Ability to disable Redwood remote admin/management for their tenant
4) Procurement asking for 35% first-year discount

Recommendations from my side: we can commit to US-only storage for a Dedicated deployment (we already offer region pinning) but we should not grant unrestricted onsite audits or eliminate remote management entirely without controls. Procurement ask on discount is material and needs Deal Desk / Exec approval.

Marissa/Rishi — can you take the legal/terms and pricing perspective? I think this needs a quick exec decision so we don't lose momentum — Finoworks is targeting procurement sign-off by 11/05.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: RE: Private deployment — data residency & audit scope questions

Karthik — thanks for the heads up and for forwarding the RFP. I reviewed the attachment and talked to Security/Infra: 

- US-only residency: we can add a contractual Data Residency clause and ensure all customer data and backups reside in US regions. We will include region pinning and a clause prohibiting cross-border replication without written consent.
- Audit rights: we cannot agree to unfettered onsite audits or full host-level access. Proposed compromise: allow a scoped audit that consists of (a) SOC2 Type II report review, (b) an in-person evidence review in a controlled room (no host access), and (c) a short technical attestation from our infra team covering controls relevant to Finoworks' use case. We can memorialize this as a limited audit addendum.
- Remote management: we can offer reduced admin privileges and an option to disable certain remote debugging consoles, but we must retain emergency remote access for incident response, subject to escalation procedures and joint-notice windows.

Pricing: procurement's 35% ask is outside standard guardrails for Dedicated. Deal Desk (Rishi) — do you have flexibility? If we need to route to Execs, propose we offer 18–22% for a 3-year commit with specific SLA and onboarding milestones.

I've attached redline markup of the MSA and a SOC2 evidence summary for their review. We should escalate the audit/disability of remote management decision to execs (CRO/CFO/CISO) because this is a permanent concession.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Finoworks_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf; SOC2_evidence_summary.xlsx
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:18:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private deployment — data residency & audit scope questions

Team — after reviewing Marissa's note and the redlines, here's the executive decision and the conditional path forward we can offer Finoworks:

1) Data residency: APPROVED. We will contractually guarantee US-only data storage & backups for the Dedicated deployment. Add language that prevents cross-border replication unless both parties agree in writing.

2) Audit rights: PARTIAL APPROVAL. We cannot permit unrestricted onsite host-level audits. Approved approach: Finoworks may (a) review our SOC2 Type II report and related evidence, (b) conduct a controlled, in-person evidence review at a Redwood facility or designated shared facility (no host/root access), and (c) request a targeted attestation covering controls that map to their risk areas. This will be the contractual audit addendum.

3) Remote management restrictions: CONDITIONAL APPROVAL. We will support disabling non-essential remote admin consoles for the customer's tenant after onboarding completion, provided the contract includes: (a) an emergency remote access clause limited to incident response with 24–48 hour advance notice where possible, (b) a mutual change-control process, and (c) a 12‑month pilot period after which we revisit. Full, permanent removal of emergency access is declined — too high operational risk.

4) Pricing concession: APPROVED AT LIMIT. We can offer a 20% first-year discount (instead of 35%) bundled with a 3-year committed term and success milestones (SLA acceptance, completion of security onboarding within 45 days). Any deeper discount requires CFO sign-off.

Please prepare a contract amendment and updated MSA redline reflecting these terms. Karthik — share this decision with Finoworks and ask procurement to confirm whether the 20% plus the audit compromise and remote-management terms are acceptable. Include DocuSign link once redlines are finalized.

Laura Bennett
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
